claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let's start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I do have a child I'm responsible for. I have one child - Alex, who is 17 years old and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. So you have one child, Alex, who is 17 years old and lives with you at home.

Since Alex is 17, I need to understand their current situation to determine eligibility. For children aged 16-19, they need to be in approved education or training to qualify for Child Benefit.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, studying at school, college, doing A-levels, or in an approved training program)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in any approved education at the moment. They left school but haven't started any college courses or anything like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that Alex left school and isn't currently in approved education or training.

I have one more important question to determine eligibility:

**Has Alex started paid work for 24 hours or more per week, or started claiming any benefits in their own right** (such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work that many hours - they're not working 24 hours a week or anything like that. And they don't claim any benefits in their own name either.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. Let me also ask:

**Did Alex register with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services when they left education?** 

(This is important because if a 16 or 17 year old leaves education or training and registers with these services, you can continue to receive Child Benefit for up to 20 weeks)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not sure about that - I don't know if they've registered with a careers service or anything like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for being honest about what you know. Let me ask you a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

**Do you live in the UK?**

## Assessment Result

Based on the information you've provided, I'm unable to make a definitive determination about your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex. Here's why:

**For Alex (age 17):**

Normally, Child Benefit continues for children aged 16-19 if they're in approved education or training. Since Alex has left school and isn't currently in approved education or training, this would typically mean Child Benefit would stop.

**However**, there's an important exception: If a 16 or 17 year old leaves education or training and registers with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services, Child Benefit can continue for up to 20 weeks.

Since you're not sure whether Alex has registered with a careers service, I cannot definitively tell you whether you're eligible or not.

**What you should do:**

1. **Find out if Alex registered** with a careers service or the armed services when they left education
2. **Contact HMRC's Child Benefit Office** directly to discuss Alex's specific situation - they can access your records and provide definitive guidance

If Alex hasn't registered with a careers service and isn't planning to return to approved education or training, your Child Benefit entitlement for Alex may have ended when they left education.
